LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The top-level/global scope of this PKGBUILD consists solely of standard variable definitions and array assignments: `pkgname`, `pkgver`, `pkgrel`, `pkgdesc`, `arch`, `url`, `license`, `depends`, `provides`, `conflicts`, `_release`, `source`, `noextract`, and `sha256sums`. None of these contain command substitution (neither backticks nor `$(...)`), `eval`, `base64`, `curl`, `wget`, or any other construct that would execute code during sourcing. The `source` array entries are plain strings using only variable interpolation (`$pkgver`, `$_release`, `$url`), not command execution. `makepkg --printsrcinfo` only sources the PKGBUILD to print `.SRCINFO` metadata; it does not download sources or run `pkgver()`, `prepare()`, `build()`, or `package()`. The `source` URLs point to the package's own upstream GitHub repository (KopyTKG/spot), which is expected. The `package()` function (which contains the install/cp operations) is out of scope for this gate since it is not executed during `--printsrcinfo`.
</details>
<summary>
No top-level code execution during sourcing; standard PKGBUILD metadata only.
</summary>
</security_assessment>

+ Initial PKGBUILD audit complete -- No top-level code execution during sourcing; standard PKGBUILD metadata only.

There are no eval, curl, wget, base64, or other dangerous commands; no obfuscation; no exfiltration; no modification of unrelated system files; and no post-install hooks. Downloading a prebuilt binary from the project's own GitHub releases is consistent with the package's stated purpose and is not evidence of malice.
